description: Optional `fields` input on my_portfolio, market_snapshot, user_profile. An array of dotted paths — the server prunes the response to only those paths. Agents that only need one or two fields out of a large response should always use this.

syntax.meaning: Keep the top-level field `foo` (and everything under it).
Keep only `foo.bar`; siblings of `bar` are dropped.
Keep the array `foo`, every element in full.
Keep the array `foo`, but only `bar` on each element.
Multiple `[]` levels are supported for nested arrays.

notes: Path resolution is lenient against data: a path that refers to a field which is None / absent silently drops — legitimate when an account has no positions, or the subscription is empty.
Path resolution is strict against syntax: empty paths, leading/trailing dots, leading brackets (`[].foo`), indexed bracket access (`foo[0]`) all return a tool error.

Type-mismatch paths drop silently (not an error): `foo[]` against a non-array `foo`, or `foo.bar` against a scalar `foo`. If a projection returns less than expected, check that the path matches the response shape in describe(topic='<tool>_output').
A whole-branch path (e.g., `account`) overrides narrower sibling paths (`account.netLiq`) — the whole subtree is kept.
Empty / missing `fields` returns the full response — no projection, same as before Phase 11.
